title: Refusal Direction as a Cheap Detector That Breaks: Replicating the Probe Cliff Without Training

original_idea.body: Extract the refusal direction from one open model, use the projection of prompt activations as a jailbreak-success predictor, measure detection AUC per attack family and the ID-to-OOD drop vs a trained probe.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether a free interpretability-based jailbreak detector is robust OOD, informing cheap monitoring defenses.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extract refusal direction (existing code), compute projections, measure AUC; guided white-box, single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused AUC-per-family and ID-to-OOD drop measurement; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: White-box on open weights, released code, lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Single GPU activation extraction; light probe training.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal direction and probe OOD-cliff known; the free-vs-trained comparison may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Components published; the specific projection-detector robustness comparison may be open.
